title.narrative: ERSKID/KIB: Just transitions in vulnerable places - digital solutions for more climate resilient informal areas (Namibia) and climate smart urban recovery of communities affected by crisis (Ukraine)

description.narrative:
With an overall budget of 6,000,000 Euros (BMZ contribution), this 3+-year project (November 2022 – December 2025) aims to support participating countries in promoting ‘just transitions in vulnerable places - digital solutions for more climate resilient informal areas and climate smart urban recovery of communities affected by crisis’. It builds on and supports the work and objectives of sustainable urbanisation and digital transformation projects and programmes in the respective locations, comprising of two modules:
• Module 1: Towards climate resilient neighbourhoods and communities in Namibia • Module 2: Towards inclusive, smart, and resilient urban recovery in Ukraine
In both locations, the project engages with national, sub-national and local government institutions in support of digital urban data generation and analysis for evidenced-informed and participatory decision making by application of diagnostic tools, hereby align project objectives towards localizing the 2030 Sustainable Development Agenda and the New Urban Agenda. It also builds on the most recent discussions of G7 member states on the link between climate resilience and sustainable urbanisation, the urban dimensions of the postpandemic world (#COVID), the Paris Agreement (#CLIMATE) and Sendai Framework (#CONFLICT).
The project will aim to contribute to and leverage broader initiatives focusing on the following key areas: • Reviewing of relevant urban policies at the appropriate level and provide integrated policy support (Principles: long term demographic projections, multi-level roles and responsibilities, reduced territorial disparities, jurisdictional coherence, etc.) • Reinvigorating long-term and integrated urban and territorial planning and design (Principles: scope and content of urban plans, sustainable density, and mixed use, adequate public space and street connectivity, space for a variety of economic activities, etc.) • Assessing urban legislation/ rules/ regulations and governance (Principles: definition of space under urban control, legal basis for urban planning, building rights, acquisition of public space, building codes, etc.) • Supporting effective, innovative, and sustainable financing frameworks and instruments (Principles: fiscal/ financial management cycle, capital investment plan – prioritization and planning, opportunities for increased local revenue generation, etc.) • Implementing climate resilient local innovation challenges at pilot basis (Principles: planned city extensions at appropriate scale, urban infill and retrofitting, urban reconstruction, migration dynamics, instruments for capturing public benefit of public investments, support community-led processes, etc.)
Cross-cutting elements for the UNITAC Hamburg deployment in both contexts are technical assistance and capacity development to fully embrace a multi-level whole of government approach to digital urban data generation and analysis for evidenced based decision making as well as sharing of good practices for urban innovation.
